To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the methanol administration decreased the levels of DA and NE in most of the brain areas studied, but increased DA level in striatum.

acute administration of methanol in rats decreased the levels of dopamine in striatum and hypothalamus, noradrenaline and adrenaline in all brain areas studied and increased the level of serotonin and 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid in hypothalamus and midbrain.
acute methanol administration decreased DA and NE levels, but increased 5HT level and 5 HIAA in the brain of rat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of metholol on the monoaminergic system in the rat brain.
the effect of methaol on monoamines in the central nervous system of rats.
the effect of acute methanol intoxication on brain monoaminergic systems in discrete areas of the rat brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
methanol is a potent neurotoxicant and its effects on the central monoaminergic system may be due to the inhibition of the enzyme MAO and/or inhibition of the enzyme DOPA decarboxylase.
methanol is a central nervous system depressant and its effects on brain monoamine levels are dose dependent.
methanol administration caused a significant reduction of DA level and increase of NE, E and 5 HT level in different regions of the brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

methanol administration significantly decreased DA level in striatum, hypothalamus, cortex, midbrain and cerebellum, and significantly increased it in hypothalamic area, and NE level in striatum hypothalamus and cortex, and E level in hypothalamus and midbrain, while 5HT level was significantly increased in hypothalamis and midbrain and 5 HIAA level was increased in striatum and midbrain, and significantly decreased in hypothalamus.
methanol has an effect on the central monoaminergic systems and that the effect is dependent on the dose and the brain area studied.

methanol administration caused significant alterations in the levels of monoamines in discrete areas of the brain and these changes were not only due to the effect of methanole itself, but were also influenced by the metabolic products formed in the brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of the methanol on the monoamine levels in the rat brain varies according to the region and the monoamine systems.
methanol can have a significant effect on monoamine levels in the brain and that this effect may vary depending on the brain area and the monoaminergic system involved.
the brain is a highly sensitive organ to the effects of methanol.
